title: How to Photograph Products That Will Sell for Years (Not Just This Season)
description: Some product photos age fast, others sell forever. Here's how to shoot photos that don't look dated in 3 years.

blocks.text: Some product photos age like milk. Others age like wine. The difference isn't luck—it's specific choices you can copy.
Here's how to shoot photos that still sell in 2029.
What Ages Poorly
Photo trends that date quickly:
If it's obviously "2024-style," it looks tired by 2027.
What Ages Well

items.text: Classic composition (rule of thirds, centered, clean)
Timeless props (books, plants, wood, linen, stone)

blocks.text: The photos in luxury brand catalogs 20 years ago still look premium today. Not by accident.
The Neutral Background Rule
Bold branded colors work today, but styles shift. Neutral tones (white, cream, gray, black) never date.
Compromise: Neutral primary background with subtle brand color accents that can be updated.

The Editing Restraint
Heavy editing dates faster than shooting choices. Every extreme edit (vignette, film grain, dramatic contrast) will look "of its era."
Rule: Edit toward clean and accurate. Save stylistic edits for temporary campaign versions, not primary listing photos.
The Model/Person Question
If your product photography includes people:
The 1990s photos with mall bangs and shoulder pads look painfully dated. Avoid the modern equivalent.
The Verification Test
Look at your product photos and ask: "Will this look dated in 2029?"
If it's screamingly "2024-style," expect a reshoot in 2-3 years.
If it's neutral, clean, and classical, expect it to serve for 5+ years.
